parts.name: Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.example: 0 — A reality  B truth  C fact  D existence → A
parts.title: Islands without cars
paras: Imagine a place where the loudest sound in the morning is birdsong rather than traffic. On a few small islands around the world, this is everyday (0) reality, because private cars are simply not allowed. Visitors who arrive by ferry are often surprised to find that they have to [[1]] do with bicycles, horse-drawn carts or their own two feet.

For local residents, the ban is a [[2]] of great pride. Many of them say that it has helped to [[3]] the peaceful character of their community, and that children can play outside without their parents constantly worrying about their [[4]].

Of course, life without cars is not always easy. Heavy shopping has to be carried home by hand, and in an emergency, people [[5]] on a small number of specially approved vehicles. Some younger islanders also complain that the lack of transport makes it hard to [[6]] time with friends who live at the other end of the island.

Even so, very few residents would like the rules to [[7]]. As one of them put it, 'Once you get used to the quiet, it's hard to imagine living any other way.' For tourists, too, the islands [[8]] a welcome break from the noise of modern life.

q.expl: Устойчивое выражение make do with sth — обходиться тем, что есть (хотя хотелось бы лучшего). С get/take/have такого выражения нет.
a source of pride — повод для гордости. Origin — происхождение, base — основа. Cause бывает в выражении cause for (с предлогом for, не of).
Нужен переходный глагол «сохранить что-то»: preserve the character. Remain и last не берут дополнения, hold в значении «удерживать» сюда не подходит.

worry about sb's safety — беспокоиться о чьей-то безопасности (физической, от машин, травм). Security — защита от преступлений, охрана; protection и defence — сама защита, а не состояние «быть в безопасности».
depend on — зависеть, полагаться на. Trust идёт без предлога (trust sb), believe — с in, hope — с for.
spend time with sb — проводить время с кем-то. Pass time значит «коротать время», и с with friends так не говорят.
После would like the rules to… нужен глагол без дополнения: правила change — меняются. Turn и convert требуют into, switch — to.
offer a break — дать, предложить передышку. Allow и let — «разрешать» (allow sb to do), admit — «признавать» или «впускать».

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Why do we forget?
paras: Most of us have walked into a room and immediately forgotten (0) why we went there. According to psychologists, this is not [[9]] sign that our memory is getting worse. In fact, it has [[10]] to do with age at all.

Researchers believe that doorways act [[11]] a kind of 'event boundary'. When we pass through a door, the brain files away memories of the previous room in order to make space [[12]] new information. Experiments have shown that people who walk through a doorway are more likely to forget a task [[13]] those who walk the same distance within a single room.

[[14]] this might sound frustrating, it is actually a sensible system. If we remembered every detail of our day, we would find it extremely difficult to concentrate on [[15]] we were doing. So the next time you forget why you came into the kitchen, don't panic – just go back to where you started, and the memory will probably come back [[16]] you.

q.expl: Перед исчисляемым существительным в единственном числе (sign) нужен артикль: not a sign that… — не признак того, что…
have nothing to do with — не иметь никакого отношения к. Подсказка — at all в конце: оно усиливает отрицание.
act as sth — выполнять роль, служить чем-то.
make space/room for sth — освобождать место для чего-то.
Сравнение: more likely … than those who… Слово more раньше в предложении — главная подсказка.
Уступка: Although this might sound frustrating, it is… — «хотя это может раздражать, на самом деле…». Подойдут также Though и While.
concentrate on what we were doing — сосредоточиться на том, что мы делали. What = the thing that.
come back to sb — вспомниться: the memory will come back to you.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: The rise of podcasts
paras: Over the last decade, podcasts have become (0) increasingly popular all over the world. Part of their [[17]] is that listeners can enjoy them while doing something else, like cooking or going for a run. The [[18]] of topics is also enormous: there are shows about everything from ancient history to [[19]] finance.
Many of the most successful presenters are not [[20]] broadcasters at all. They are ordinary people whose [[21]] approach to their subject makes up for any lack of experience.

However, not everyone is completely positive. Critics point out that, unlike newspapers, podcasts rarely have editors who check the [[22]] of the information, and that it is [[23]] easy to spread false claims. Listeners are therefore [[24]] to think carefully about who is speaking – and why.

q.expl: После their нужно существительное: attraction — привлекательность.
the variety of topics — разнообразие тем. Не путай с various (прилагательное) и variation (изменение, отклонение).
Перед существительным finance нужно прилагательное: personal finance — личные финансы.
Перед broadcasters нужно прилагательное: professional — профессиональные ведущие.
Перед approach нужно прилагательное: passionate — увлечённый, страстный.
После check the нужно существительное: accuracy — точность. Ловушка: inaccuracy поменяло бы смысл — редакторы проверяют точность.
Перед прилагательным easy нужно наречие: surprisingly easy — удивительно легко.
Пассив: are advised to — им советуют. Обрати внимание на написание: advice — существительное, advise — глагол.

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.
parts.example: 0 What type of music do you like best? FAVOURITE → What IS YOUR FAVOURITE type of music?

q.first: I'm sure Tom didn't break the window on purpose.
q.expl: Уверенность, что чего-то не было в прошлом: can't have + V3 — can't have broken.

q.first: I won't go to the party if you don't come with me.
q.before: I won't go to the party
q.expl: if … not ⇄ unless: unless you come = if you don't come. После unless глагол в утвердительной форме.

q.first: 'Why don't we go to the beach?' said Anna.
q.expl: suggest + -ing или suggest (that) we (should) go. Ошибка: suggested us to go — так нельзя.

q.first: People say that the hotel is haunted.
q.expl: Безличный пассив: sth is said to be… — говорят, что…

q.first: I didn't go to the concert because I was ill.
q.before: I would have gone to the concert
q.expl: Третий тип условных (нереальное прошлое): would have gone … if I hadn't been ill.

q.first: This is the first time I have been on a plane.
q.expl: This is the first time I have done… ⇄ I have never done… before.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a young woman who writes crosswords. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: The puzzle maker
parts.subtitle: At twenty-six, Elena Varga writes crosswords for a national newspaper. She explains what the job really involves.
paras: Elena Varga was nineteen when a national newspaper published her first crossword. 'I'd been sending puzzles to the editor for almost a year,' she tells me, 'and every single one came back with a polite note saying "not quite". I kept every note, though. Each one told me something about what I was doing wrong, so in a strange way they were the most useful thing I received that year.' Now twenty-six, she produces four puzzles a week and has a loyal following of solvers who write to her whenever a clue particularly delights – or annoys – them.

Her working day is far less glamorous than people imagine. She starts with the grid – the pattern of black and white squares – and then fills it with words, a process she compares to packing a suitcase. 'You always think you have plenty of room, and then you discover that the last few things simply won't fit. At that point you have to take half of it out again and start over.' Only when the grid is complete does she begin writing the clues, which is the part she enjoys most.

A good clue, she explains, has to be fair. 'The solver should be able to say "Of course!" when they finally get it, not "How was I supposed to know that?"' She tests every puzzle on her flatmate, a medical student who claims to have no interest in crosswords whatsoever. 'He's the perfect judge. If he can't work out a clue after a few minutes, it isn't clever – it's just badly written.'

Not all the feedback she receives is so gentle. Last year she accidentally used the same answer twice in one puzzle, and within hours her inbox was full. 'Some of the emails were quite rude,' she admits, 'but honestly, I was more embarrassed than hurt. People care about these puzzles. They're part of their routine – they do them on the train or with their morning coffee – and I'd let them down.'

Elena worries that crosswords are sometimes seen as a hobby for retired people. To change this, she has started running workshops in secondary schools, where she asks students to write clues about their own lives. 'The first time I did it, I expected them to be bored stiff. Instead, a girl at the back wrote a clue about her grandmother that was better than anything I've written this year.' She hopes some of them will one day send puzzles to newspapers themselves – and keep the polite rejection notes, just as she did.

q.stem: Why did Elena keep the editor's notes?
opts: She hoped to publish them one day.
She found them helpful for improving her puzzles.
She wanted to prove that she had been treated unfairly.
She was proud of having been noticed by the editor.
q.hl: Each one told me something about what I was doing wrong
q.expl: Каждая записка показывала, что она делает не так, — поэтому они были «самым полезным» за год. Об отказах как несправедливости или о гордости в тексте ничего нет.

q.stem: What does Elena mean by comparing her work to packing a suitcase?
opts: It is a task she prefers to do quickly.
It requires her to plan carefully before she begins.
It often involves undoing work and trying again.
It becomes easier the more often she does it.
q.hl: At that point you have to take half of it out again and start over.
q.expl: Последние вещи «не влезают», и приходится вынимать половину и начинать сначала — то есть переделывать работу. Про скорость, планирование заранее или то, что становится легче, она не говорит.

q.stem: Why does Elena test her puzzles on her flatmate?
opts: He is an experienced crossword solver.
He can check the accuracy of scientific clues.
He shows her whether a clue is fair to an ordinary person.
He enjoys pointing out mistakes in her work.
q.hl: If he can't work out a clue after a few minutes, it isn't clever – it's just badly written.
q.expl: Сосед не интересуется кроссвордами, поэтому он — обычный человек. Если он не может разгадать подсказку, значит, она нечестная. Ловушка B: он студент-медик, но о научных подсказках речи нет.

q.stem: How did Elena feel about the emails she received after her mistake?
opts: She thought the readers had overreacted.
She was upset that people had been so rude.
She felt she had disappointed people who relied on her.
She was surprised that so many people had noticed.
q.expl: «I'd let them down» — она подвела людей, для которых кроссворд — часть дня. Ловушка B: письма были грубыми, но она «more embarrassed than hurt» — скорее стыдно, чем обидно.

q.stem: What does Elena say about her first school workshop?
opts: The students were less interested than she had hoped.
One student's work impressed her more than she expected.
She found it difficult to explain how to write clues.
The students preferred writing about their families.
q.hl: wrote a clue about her grandmother that was better than anything
q.expl: Она ждала, что ученикам будет скучно, а одна девочка написала подсказку лучше, чем все её собственные за год. Ловушка D: подсказка была о бабушке, но о том, что все предпочли писать о семье, не сказано.

q.stem: In the article as a whole, the writer presents Elena as someone who
opts: values persistence and learning from criticism.
prefers working alone to working with others.
is more interested in teaching than in writing puzzles.
q.hl: keep the polite rejection notes, just as she did
q.expl: Через весь текст: почти год отказов, которые она хранила и на которых училась, честное отношение к критике читателей, и в конце — совет ученикам хранить отказы, как она. Успех не был лёгким (A), а школы — дополнение к работе, не главное (D).

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a man who travelled around Ireland without a smartphone. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Lost and found
parts.subtitle: Journalist Tom Reeve spent a month cycling around Ireland without a smartphone. Here is what he learned.
paras: It started as a bet. A friend claimed that nobody under thirty could find their way around a foreign country without a phone, and I was stubborn enough to try. [[37]] I packed a paper map, a compass I hadn't used since I was a scout, and a notebook for writing down directions.

The first day was a disaster. I misread the map within an hour and spent the afternoon cycling in a large circle. [[38]] By the time I realised my mistake, it was getting dark, and I had to knock on the door of a farmhouse to ask where the nearest bed and breakfast was.

That knock on the door turned out to be the best thing that happened on the whole trip. The farmer, a cheerful man called Declan, not only gave me directions but insisted that I stay for dinner. [[39]] I left the next morning with a full stomach, a hand-drawn map and the phone numbers of three of his cousins who lived further along my route.

This became the pattern for the rest of the month. Without a screen to look at, I had to talk to people, and they almost always had time for me. [[40]] An elderly woman in a post office spent twenty minutes explaining a shortcut; a group of teenagers cycled alongside me for several miles to make sure I didn't miss a turning.

Of course, there were moments when I would have given anything for a phone. On one particularly wet afternoon, I couldn't find the hostel I had booked, and there was nobody around to ask. [[41]] It was the only night of the trip when I felt genuinely miserable.
Since coming home, I have gone back to using my phone, but I use it differently. [[42]] I've realised that getting slightly lost is often the quickest way to find something worth seeing.

sents.A: So, a few weeks later, I said goodbye to my phone and booked a ferry ticket.
sents.B: Worse still, I passed the same petrol station three times without noticing.
sents.C: Over a huge plate of stew, he told me about every village between his farm and the coast.
sents.D: Some went to quite extraordinary lengths to help.
sents.E: In the end, I slept in a bus shelter, wrapped in every piece of clothing I owned.
sents.F: These days, I only switch on the navigation app when I really need it.
sents.G: Declan and I still exchange letters a couple of times a year.

q.expl: Перед пропуском — пари, после — «I packed a paper map…». Нужен переход от решения к поездке: «So, a few weeks later… booked a ferry ticket» (A).
«Worse still» продолжает список неудач первого дня, а «three times without noticing» объясняет следующую фразу «By the time I realised my mistake» (B).

Фермер пригласил на ужин → «Over a huge plate of stew, he told me about every village» (C). Отсюда потом и «hand-drawn map». Ловушка G: про письма Деклану логично в конце, но там нет пропуска для неё.
«Some went to quite extraordinary lengths to help» (D), а дальше — два примера: женщина на почте и подростки на велосипедах. Some отсылает к people из предыдущего предложения.
Не нашёл хостел, спросить некого → «In the end, I slept in a bus shelter» (E). Следующее предложение «the only night… miserable» описывает именно эту ночь.
«I use it differently» — а как именно? «I only switch on the navigation app when I really need it» (F).

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four students describe where they like to study. For questions 43–52, choose from the students (A–D). The students may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: My favourite place to study

texts.name: Lena
texts.body: I've always studied at the city library, mainly because I can't concentrate at home – my little brothers are far too noisy. The reading room on the top floor is my favourite spot. It's silent, of course, but what I really like is that everyone around me is working too. If I see someone next to me reading a huge textbook, I feel guilty about checking my messages and get back to work. The only downside is that the library closes at seven, so in exam season I sometimes have to leave just when I'm finally getting into it. I've asked the staff whether they could stay open later, but apparently there isn't enough money.

texts.name: Marcus
texts.body: People are often surprised that I revise in a busy café, but total silence actually makes me nervous – I start noticing every little sound. In a café, the background noise blends into one comfortable hum. I usually go to the same place near the station, and the staff know my order by now. I'll be honest: it isn't the cheapest way to study, because I feel I have to buy something every hour or so to justify taking up a table. Last year I worked out that I'd spent more on coffee than on books! Still, my grades went up, so I think it was worth it.

texts.name: Sofia
texts.body: I study in my bedroom, at a desk my dad and I built together from an old door. It's not the most comfortable set-up in the world, but I love being able to organise everything exactly the way I want – my notes are colour-coded and stuck all over the wall. The hardest thing is staying away from my bed, which is about a metre behind me! I've found that the only solution is to study in fifty-minute blocks with a proper break in between. I set an alarm, and when it goes off, I make myself get up and walk round the garden, even if it's raining.

texts.name: Ravi
texts.body: For me, studying alone has never worked. A few friends and I meet three evenings a week at the community centre, which has a room that anyone can book for free. We each work on our own subjects, but whenever someone gets stuck, there's always somebody who can explain it. At first, I was worried we'd just end up chatting, and to be fair, in the first couple of weeks that's exactly what happened. Now we have a rule: no talking about anything other than work until eight o'clock. I've learned more from explaining things to the others than from any textbook.

q.hl: total silence actually makes me nervous
q.expl: Маркус: полная тишина его нервирует, он начинает замечать каждый звук. Ловушка A: Лена любит тишину библиотеки.

q.stem: describes a rule that changed how a group behaves?
q.expl: Рави: сначала группа болтала, теперь есть правило — до восьми говорить только о работе.

q.stem: is motivated by seeing other people working hard?
q.hl: If I see someone next to me reading a huge textbook, I feel guilty
q.expl: Лене стыдно отвлекаться, когда рядом кто-то читает огромный учебник. Ловушка D: Рави тоже занимается не один, но его мотивирует не это.

q.stem: has to resist the temptation to rest?
q.hl: The hardest thing is staying away from my bed
q.expl: Софии труднее всего не лечь на кровать, которая прямо за спиной.

q.stem: wishes their place of study were open for longer?
q.expl: Библиотека закрывается в семь, и Лена просила продлить часы работы.

q.stem: admits that their way of studying costs quite a lot?
q.hl: it isn't the cheapest way to study
q.expl: Маркус каждый час что-то покупает, а за год потратил на кофе больше, чем на книги. Ловушка D: комнату в центре можно бронировать бесплатно.

q.stem: uses a piece of furniture they helped to make?
q.hl: a desk my dad and I built together from an old door
q.expl: София с папой сделала стол из старой двери.

q.stem: believes that helping others has improved their own learning?
q.expl: Рави: «I've learned more from explaining things to the others than from any textbook».

q.stem: had doubts at first about whether their method would work?
q.hl: At first, I was worried we'd just end up chatting
q.expl: Рави боялся, что они будут просто болтать, и первые недели так и было.

q.stem: can see that their method has had a positive effect on their results?
q.expl: Маркус: «my grades went up, so I think it was worth it».
